test_title: PYST 52: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 21 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In 2025, India launched Operation SINDOOR in response to a terror attack. The operation targeted terrorist camps in which region?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan and Pakistan occupied Kashmir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation SINDOOR** was a high-stakes military counter-terrorism operation launched by the **Indian Armed Forces** in the year **2025**.
 
• The operation was initiated as a direct **retaliatory response** to a major **terror attack** targeting Indian security installations, aiming to dismantle the infrastructure of terror.
 
• The primary targets of this operation were identified as **terrorist training camps** and active **launch pads** located deep within **Pakistan** and across the **Line of Control (LoC)** in **Pakistan occupied Kashmir (PoK)**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Pakistan and Pakistan occupied Kashmir.***
 
• This mission utilized **advanced surveillance** and **precision-strike capabilities** to ensure maximum impact on the terror modules while minimizing collateral damage.
 
• The execution of **Operation SINDOOR** reflects India’s evolved **military doctrine** of proactive deterrence, shifting from a defensive posture to one of "pre-emptive" strikes against cross-border threats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pakistan occupied Kashmir (PoK)**:
 
 
• **PoK** is a region that has been under the administrative control of **Pakistan** since the **1947** conflict, but is considered an integral part of **India** by the Indian government.
 
• It consists of two main administrative parts: **Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK)** and **Gilgit-Baltistan**.
 
• The region is strategically significant due to its **geographical location**, sharing borders with **Afghanistan** and **China**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Counter-Terror Operations**:
 
 
• **2016 Surgical Strikes**: Conducted by the **Indian Army** in response to the **Uri attack**, targeting launch pads in **PoK**.
 
• **Operation Bandar (2019)**: An aerial strike conducted by the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** on a **Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM)** camp in **Balakot**, located in the **Khyber Pakhtunkhwa** province of **Pakistan**.
 
• These operations signify the **"New India"** policy of providing a "befitting reply" to acts of **state-sponsored terrorism**.
 
 
 
• **Tactical Significance**:
 
 
• Modern operations like **Operation SINDOOR** often involve the use of **Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs)**, **Electronic Warfare (EW)**, and **satellite imagery** provided by **ISRO** for pinpoint accuracy.
 
• Such strikes are intended to disrupt the **logistics** and **communication channels** of extremist organizations like **Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT)** and **JeM**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geopolitical Context**: The launch of **Operation SINDOOR** in **2025** occurred amidst heightening tensions and was justified under the **Right to Self-Defense** as per **Article 51** of the **United Nations Charter**.
 
• **Line of Control (LoC)**: The **LoC** serves as the de facto border between **India** and **Pakistan** in the region of **Jammu and Kashmir**, and most cross-border operations are focused on this **740-km long** boundary.
 
• **Strategic Impact**: Beyond the immediate destruction of camps, such operations serve as a **psychological deterrent** and demonstrate **technological superiority** in the **South Asian** theater.
